pillar_reactions.evidence: Engaged on mechanics rather than value. He asked whether calisthenics was in scope before the pillar was even presented — 'I don't know if you guys have any friends that specialize in calisthenics as well, because that would be quite...' — and got '60 to 70 percent kettlebells, 30 to 40 percent calisthenics'. When mobility landed he completed the rep's sentence with its purpose: 'Yeah, so for joints.'

Accepted the eat-for-health philosophy without argument, then worked through the practicalities in detail: whether the plan covers food ('I don't have a chef but in Moscow it's relatively simple... special kitchens that you just tell them what'), how restaurants fit, then alcohol ('The other question I had was alcohol') and drugs. He was mapping the programme onto his actual life, which is a buying behaviour, but every question was logistics rather than substance.

The 24-7 support and weekly plan adaptation were described and drew a flat 'understood, cool' and 'Cool. So, you know.' The one part that visibly landed was the education endgame, which he had already absorbed from the free content: 'I actually heard that in one of his videos. Where by the end of it, you effectively can train someone else if you want.' Accountability itself, the pillar most relevant to a man whose stated problem is never starting, drew no reaction at all.

anchors.raw: Also, finances are not an issue, so I'm prepared to spend whatever it takes to achieve what I want.
anchors.note: Volunteered at 00:08, fifteen minutes before any number was named. The strongest supportive anchor in the batch — and it was left entirely unused. With the budget objection pre-removed, the whole of the discovery process was available at no risk and none of it was run.

anchors.raw: I've had, and I always have, personal trainers, that's not an issue. As I said, finances are not a restriction in this sense
anchors.note: He is a habitual buyer of one-to-one coaching, so $6,000 is a category he already spends in. His complaint about them is structural, not financial — 'everybody's quite niched and tailored' with no overall plan — which is precisely the differentiation the offer could have been sold on.

anchors.raw: I saw him on Instagram... I found the video stuff that he did very, very easily to consume, quite easy to consume in terms of like as instruction
anchors.note: Arrived pre-sold on the coach personally, including the physique ('I quite like the physique that Trevor has') and the six-month education endgame he had already heard on a video. The content did the selling; the call only had to not break it.

unmet_demand.want: Help getting off nicotine — he raised it unprompted: 'I'm trying to cut this stuff off as well but it's, you know, I need the nicotine'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer covers kettlebells, nutrition and mobility. Nicotine cessation is outside all three and the rep closed the topic rather than exploring it: 'I hear you brother, don't worry about it.'

unmet_demand.want: A master plan that his other specialists can feed into, rather than another niched coach — 'I quite like the idea of creating an overall plan and then feed onto it'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is the closest thing to a stated buying criterion on the call and it was never addressed. It is genuinely unclear whether Trevor's programme would direct or absorb the personal trainers the prospect already employs, or simply replace them.

unmet_demand.want: A screening answer on whether high-intensity ballistic training is appropriate for a detrained 43-year-old with a 27-year smoking history
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He never asked, and nobody offered. There is no clinical screening step anywhere in the offer, so the question could not have been answered even if raised.
